mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate exhibits a negative correlation with S&P 500 20-day forward returns, so a lower rate predicts positive returns. This is because lower rates reduce the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, increasing present value.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% are not significantly positive compared to the baseline (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a tightening monetary policy that increases discount rates and compresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL > 0.5% MoM) and unemployment (UNRATE > 0.2pp MoM) signals an economic slowdown that increases equity risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition (CPIAUCSL > 212.0 AND UNRATE > 7.5) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 210.0), the S&P 500 tends to underperform in the short term due to central bank tightening and reduced consumer spending power.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when CPIAUCSL > 210.0 are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The level of housing starts (HOUST) has a positive correlation with S&P 500 20-day forward returns, so a higher HOUST predicts positive returns. This is because strong housing activity signals a robust economy and increased consumer confidence.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns in periods when HOUST is above its 1-year moving average are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100, it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that increases recession risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when INDPRO < 100 are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.0%) and low retail sales (RSAFS < 340000) signals a weak labor market and reduced consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days.
regime_hint: weak labor and consumer demand regime
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns in periods meeting the trigger condition (UNRATE > 7.0 AND RSAFS < 340000) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 7.0%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform in the short term due to reduced consumer spending and increased economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns in periods when UNRATE > 7.0 are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
